$comment: Defects and traps in the original data files. Every entry is applied by a reader at read time; no original file is ever edited. `kind` is one of: `metadata` (an attribute states something untrue), `trap` (the file is correct but a natural way of reading it gives a wrong answer), `truncated` (content is missing), `superseded` (a better copy of the same submission exists elsewhere), `naming` (the same thing has different names in different places). `status` is `confirmed` when the evidence is in this repository and reproducible, `unverified` otherwise. Paths are relative to data/original/.

corrections.as_shipped: Calendar year (positive = CE, negative = BCE)
corrections.correct: Year offset from 2000 CE, which the protocol defines as model year 0
corrections.evidence: `time` is days since 2000-01-01 on a 365-day calendar, and time/365 equals `year` to 2e-12 over all 463 steps: time[-1] = 365000 days where year[-1] = 1000. Read as a calendar year the first step would be 122000 BCE, which is 124 ka before present, not the 122 ka the protocol prescribes in section 2.2.2. The compliance checker deliberately requires different wording on the output `year` variable.
corrections.action: Report the variable as an offset from 2000 CE. Never convert it as a calendar year.

corrections.correct: Zero is a real value meaning no ice, not a missing value
corrections.evidence: A default netCDF4 read returns a masked array in which every ice-free cell is masked, and xarray turns those into NaN. At the last time step of ICE-6G_D that is 117051 of 131841 cells. A load or a mass integral built from such an array is NaN or silently excludes the ocean.
corrections.action: Call `Dataset.set_auto_mask(False)` on every read, or `mask_and_scale=False` in xarray. This is a standing rule in AGENTS.md and is tested.

corrections.as_shipped: Merge: BedMachine Greenland (28-Jul-2022, v5.5), BedMachine Greenland (28-Jul-2022, v5.5), GEBCO (downloaded June 2025)
corrections.correct: The first of the two Greenland entries should name the Antarctic dataset, BedMachine Antarctica v3
corrections.evidence: The three topography files differ only in their Antarctic source, and the filename records it correctly. The Bedmap2 and Bedmap3 files name their Antarctic dataset correctly in the same attribute, so this affects one file only.
corrections.action: Take the Antarctic dataset from the filename, never from the attribute.

corrections.as_shipped: crs
corrections.correct: No variable named `crs` exists in any of the three files
corrections.evidence: A CF compliance checker flags a grid_mapping attribute that names a variable the file does not contain. The coordinates are plain geographic latitude and longitude, so nothing is actually ambiguous.
corrections.action: Ignore the attribute. Treat the axes as geographic degrees.

corrections.as_shipped: Filename says GLAC3c_profile1; title and source say GLAC3c_merge1; the protocol experiment table says GLAC3b (Profile 1)
corrections.correct: The delivered files are the intended inputs. Holly Han, the lead of the protocol, confirmed on 2026-09-12 that each file combines GLAC3 versions a, b and c, with different versions for different ice sheets.
corrections.evidence: Protocol v2.4 experiment table, rows Exp03, Exp04 and Exp09 to Exp11. The compliance checker adds a fourth spelling, expecting iceHistory-GLAC3b_profile1_122ka.nc. The answer of the organisers is recorded in README.md, section "Correspondence about the GIAMIP inputs".
corrections.action: Record the delivered filename in the case file, and give the ice history as GLAC3_p1, GLAC3_p2 or GLAC3_p3, with no version letter.

corrections.as_shipped: 360 rows on linspace(180, 0, 360), dated 2017-11-15
corrections.correct: Use l721j256/A_fig10_SBK.dat from martinec2018/sbk_benchmark_data.tar.gz: 721 rows on a 0.25 degree grid, dated 2018-01-15
corrections.evidence: Z_SK_load_diff.out has 721 rows on the same 0.25 degree descending grid as the superseding file, and is dated 2018-01-17. Subtracting it from that file with no interpolation reconstructs VEGA to a maximum of 1.7e-4 m and an RMS of 2.3e-5 m against the reconstruction from GA, which is print precision. The shipped 360-row file is on a different grid and cannot be the same submission. One consequence: the figure shipped in the archive draws the old SK profile in its left panel and the new SK difference in its right panel.
corrections.action: Read the superseding file. Treat the shipped one as a stale copy.

corrections.as_shipped: Descending, from 180 to 0
corrections.correct: Every other file in the same directory ascends from 0 to 180
corrections.evidence: Z_GA, Z_GS, Z_KS, Z_VB, Z_VK and both Z_WW difference files ascend; the SK and YS files descend. numpy.interp requires an ascending first argument and returns wrong values, with no warning, when given a descending one.
corrections.action: Sort by colatitude on read, or subtract on the shared grid without interpolating. Every reader returns an ascending axis.

corrections.as_shipped: Fortran D exponents, for example -0.3024125086287D+03
corrections.correct: The same numbers with an E exponent
corrections.evidence: numpy.loadtxt raises `could not convert string '-0.3024125086287D+03' to float64`. awk, which the original GMT scripts used, accepts the leading digits and silently drops the exponent, so a naive re-run of those scripts plots this contributor 1000 times too small. Most YS files of cases B to E use the same notation, and so do the copies in resultsA_2026/ and resultsB_2026/.
corrections.action: Replace D with E before parsing.

corrections.as_shipped: The values as the contributor submitted them
corrections.correct: The published figure plots 9/10 of column 2 and 2/3 of column 4
corrections.evidence: resultsA_2026/figZ_uvf_load_diff.gmt applies `9*$2/10` to the vertical displacement difference in panel 2 and `2*$4/3` to the geoid difference in panel 4. No other series in any of the four scripts carries a rescaling of this kind; the only other arithmetic is division by the surface gravity 9.8155 to turn a potential into a geoid height. The reason for the two factors is not recorded in the script or in the paper.
corrections.action: A redraw of published figure 3 must apply both factors to reproduce the figure. A comparison against the data must not: use the columns as submitted, and treat the discrepancy the factors imply as unexplained until the contributor confirms it.

corrections.as_shipped: Different contributors store the geoid with opposite signs, and two store the gravitational potential
corrections.correct: Positive geoid height, upward
corrections.evidence: Decoded from the plotting scripts by scripts/decode_gmt_layouts.py. For benchmark A, four series are plotted as they stand: A-fig10-TABOO_256.dat column 7, A_fig10_YS.dat column 5, caseA_0.25.lmax256_GA.dat column 6, and Z_ZM_load.out column 5, which holds the gravitational potential and is divided by the surface gravity 9.8155. Six are negated: A_fig10_KS_256.dat column 5, A_fig10_SBK.dat column 4, case_A_VILMA_uve.dat column 4, fig10_n_VB_256.dat column 2, n_10ka.dat column 2, and n_10ka_axi.dat column 2, which is both negated and divided by 9.8155.
corrections.action: Take the sign and any division by gravity from gia_mip/resources/column_layouts.json, never by assumption. A reader that guesses is wrong by a factor of minus one for six of the ten benchmark A contributors, and by a factor of 9.8155 for two.

corrections.field: the geoid panel of every cross-section script, after the per-file signs of benchmarkA-geoid-sign-varies are applied
corrections.as_shipped: The panel labelled N(theta,t) holds minus the geoid displacement. The scripts agree with each other on this sign and disagree with the paper.
corrections.correct: Geoid displacement N, positive upward, as eq. 9 of the paper defines it: N = -Phi / g0.
corrections.evidence: Two independent checks. First, from the data alone: on the case C basin profile, S = -N + h_UF at every colatitude to the last stored digit, with the stored h_UF(15 kyr) = -25.72346 m, while eq. 6 and eq. 8 of the paper give S = N + h_UF over the ocean. Second, from the physics of the earth model: 1 + k is positive at every epoch for M3-L70-V01, 0.756 at the elastic limit and 0.0157 at the fluid limit, the latter set by the elastic lithosphere, so a positive surface load raises the geoid at every time. The shipped benchmark A reference is -7.38 m at the cap centre, and its magnitude lies between the elastic value of +40.6 m and the fluid value of +1.23 m computed with radopt, which is where 10 kyr belongs. The origin is visible in the layout table: the scripts draw the VEGA potential column as $5/9.8155, with no minus sign, and vega_seven_column_format names column 5 the gravitational potential increment.
corrections.action: Negate the geoid after the per-file sign of column_layouts.json has been applied. scripts/convert_martinec2018.py does this, so every N in data/converted/martinec2018/ is positive upward and agrees with docs/reference/conventions.qmd. A reader of the original files that follows the scripts alone is wrong by a factor of minus one.

corrections.as_shipped: A complete VEGA profile for benchmark A at 0.125 degree spacing, 1441 rows.
corrections.correct: It is a different run from the one behind published figure 3 and the shipped difference files
corrections.evidence: Recomputing each contributor's difference against this file misses the shipped difference file by an RMS of 0.0551 to 0.0574 m for GA, GS, KS and WW alike; the near-equality across four independent codes places the discrepancy in this file. Against the reconstruction from those same contributors it differs by a smooth bump centred on the cap edge: 0.023 m RMS inside 5 degrees, 0.474 m RMS between 9 and 11 degrees, peaking at 0.5615 m at exactly 10.00 degrees, and 0.003 m beyond 90 degrees. A least squares fit of a constant plus cos(colatitude), which is what a degree 0 and degree 1 difference would look like, explains 1.5 per cent of the variance, so this is not the degree-2 start the paper records for benchmark A in section 4.1. Section 5.1 states that the cap edge has infinite slope and converges extremely slowly with increasing cut-off degree, which is where a difference of this shape would come from. Two further checks. Both files obey the same internal relations exactly: column 6 equals minus column 5 divided by 9.8155, and column 7 equals column 6 minus column 2. So the surviving single row is genuine, internally consistent VEGA output and not a corrupted fragment, and the two files are the same quantity computed twice. And at the cap edge the eight contributors span 1.354 m, from -47.83 for SK to -49.18 for YS, with a median of -49.023. The published reference sits 0.279 m below that median and the supplied file 0.283 m above it, so both lie inside the spread, on opposite sides. Beyond colatitude 14 both agree with the median to 0.01 m. martinec2018/resultsA_2026/Z_ZM_load.out is byte-identical to this file (SHA-256 ff99f78c0aea2532b96e7d63522c7a13021e05a9843ec4a1df363d78fb4d1660), so the archive Martinec sent in September 2026 carries the second run under the original filename.
corrections.action: Do not use this file as the reference for scoring against the published difference files. Recover the reference as a contributor's profile minus its own difference file: GA, GS, KS, VK and WW agree to better than 1e-3 m over the whole range and give -302.59759412 m at colatitude 0, the value of the one-row VEGA file in the first case A archive. Keep this file as a second VEGA run, useful for judging how much the cap-edge representation moves the answer. Its header is the only record of the seven-column VEGA format and is transcribed into column_layouts.json.
corrections.open_question: Martinec wrote on 2026-09-11 that the single-row file was 'incomplete (and incorrect)', that the error arose when he renamed the file, and that the attached file is the correct original. The first half is certain. The second does not fit the arithmetic: the surviving row is exactly the value every shipped difference file was computed against, to eight decimal places across five independent codes. If the supplied file is the correct reference, then the difference files in the archive are stale and the right-hand panels of published figure 3 are wrong by up to 0.56 m at the cap edge, which is a third of that panel's plotted range. Put to him on 2026-09-11.

corrections.as_shipped: The copy in T01-03/ stops at harmonic degree 256 and has 2560 rows in each .res file
corrections.correct: Not established. The copy in T01-03/PAPER/ carries degree 257 as well, 2570 rows in each .res file, and different values
corrections.evidence: Nine of VB's tidal Love number files exist twice, once in T01-03/ and once in T01-03/PAPER/. The .ela and .flu copies differ by one row: PAPER adds degree 257, for example `257 0.70665666E-02` in h_T_T01-03_VB.ela. The .res copies differ in value as well: 8 of the first 2295 rows differ, by up to 1.07 in the residue. Every other data file in T01-03 is byte identical between the two directories, so this is not a wholesale re-run of the test.
corrections.action: Name the directory in the case file. Do not glob T01-03 for a file that exists in both, and do not assume the PAPER copy is the published one until the redraw of the published figure settles it.

corrections.as_shipped: The copy in T01-05/ and the copy in T01-05/PAPER/ have the same 603 lines and different numbers in every one of them. The working copy holds the column of k_L_T01-05_VK.dat as it stands, which is -(1 + k).
corrections.correct: The copy in T01-05/PAPER/ holds k, and it is the one the paper used.
corrections.evidence: k_L_T01-05_VK.dat is the same file in both directories. Replaying T01-05/PAPER/filter.f90 on it reproduces the working copy exactly, and gives the PAPER copy as -1 minus the column to 5e-9. The PAPER copy agrees with GS's k of test 5/1 to 9.4e-3 at degrees 2 to 9, and the working copy misses it by 0.88 to 0.93. T01-05/PAPER/love_PAP.gmt, the script of figure 6, reads the PAPER copy. The length of day of figure 13c, T02-03/lod_VK.dat, is (1 + k_2) times 75.403 ms to 1.6e-6 ms with k_2 from the PAPER copy, and misses by 67 ms with the working copy. The other 40 data files of T01-05 that exist in both directories are byte identical.
corrections.action: Read T01-05/PAPER/k_L_T01-05_VK.mod and the other files that T01-05/PAPER/love_PAP.gmt draws. Do not read the working copy.

corrections.as_shipped: The case files list BL, GS, PG, VK and ZM for test 2/1 and BL, GS, PG and VK for test 2/2, from the paper's table 1
corrections.correct: The archive holds data for GS and VK only in both tests
corrections.evidence: The GMT scripts of T02-01 and T02-02 draw two series per panel, one from the per-epoch files disp_t*_cap.dat and disp_t*_disc.dat and one from ./output_sec2parab/ and ./output_sec2disc/, attributed to GS and VK by the banner comments and by the header of u2cost.dat, which reads `performed by spectral FE code, Klemann at GFZ`. No file anywhere in the archive is attributable to BL, PG or, for these two tests, ZM.
corrections.action: Score against GS and VK for these two tests. A contributor named in the case file with no data in the archive must fail loudly, not be skipped. The gap is closed by Sia Ghelichkhani's decision of 2026-09-15: the archive is the reference data, and ZM's values in tables 10 to 12 and BL's and PG's curves in figure 12 exist only in the paper.

corrections.as_shipped: GS writes one file per epoch and VK writes one column per epoch
corrections.correct: Both hold the epochs 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10 kyr. GS also ships a run at 1000 kyr, which VK does not
corrections.evidence: GS ships disp_t0_cap.dat, disp_t1_cap.dat, disp_t2_cap.dat, disp_t5_cap.dat, disp_t10_cap.dat and disp_t1000_cap.dat, each with colatitude in column 1 and the three quantities in columns 2, 3 and 5. Column 4 is read by no panel of the published figure. VK ships u2cost.dat, v2cost.dat and e2cost.dat, each with colatitude in column 1 and one column per epoch in columns 2 to 6, as the file header states: `# Epoch (kyr): 0 1 2 5 10`. Its README adds that *cost.dat is the fine grid and *costg.dat the global one, and that the poles are omitted.
corrections.action: The reader presents both as colatitude by epoch. Do not assume that the three quantities are columns 2, 3 and 4 of the GS files: the geoid is column 5.

corrections.as_shipped: Each contributor's Love numbers of tests 2/1 and 3/1 exist twice: a signed table in the .dat file, and a plotting copy split into .ela, .flu and .res files. The .res files hold the absolute value of every residue, one (degree, residue) pair per line, and start with a line such as `*** RESIDUES   # File <<l.dat>>` that is not a comment.
corrections.correct: The signed residues are in the .dat file.
corrections.evidence: Measured on the 18 .res files of GS, RR and VB in T01-02 and T01-03: no .res value is negative, while the .dat residues carry both signs, and GS's .res files have 12 lines per degree (3060 for 255 degrees), the Maxwell modes included. The .ela and .flu copies keep the sign: every value equals the .dat value, so they are not covered here. Residues read from .res reconstruct h, which has residues of one sign, and give l and k wrong in the fluid limit h_f = h_e - sum r_j / s_j.
corrections.action: Read the .dat file. The converter reads no .ela, .flu or .res file.

corrections.as_shipped: Twelve residues per degree, `(Including the Maxwell ones)` in the header, while the relaxation spectrum spec_T01_01_GS.dat has nine modes
corrections.correct: Residue positions 6, 9 and 12 (columns 9, 12 and 15) are Maxwell modes of vanishing strength. The other nine pair, in order, with the nine columns of spec_T01_01_GS.dat.
corrections.evidence: With positions 6, 9 and 12 dropped, h_f = h_e - sum r_j / s_j holds to 1e-5 relative at every degree of all six files. At degree 2 the dropped values are of order 1e-29. At degree 128 a real mode has a residue of -1.4e-14, as small as a Maxwell mode in relative terms, so a drop by magnitude removes a real mode there.
corrections.action: Drop the residues by fixed position, never by magnitude.

corrections.as_shipped: The .mod files that the published figure of test 1/1 draws hold, per degree, one line per mode with a positive number, for example `2 0.27612688E+08`
corrections.correct: The number is the relaxation time tau_j in years. The relaxation frequency in 1/kyr is s_j = -1000 / tau_j, which is what the .dat files hold.
corrections.evidence: For GS, -1000 / tau_j from spec_T01_01_GS.mod equals the s_j of spec_T01_01_GS.dat to 3e-8 relative at every degree, and the slowest degree-2 mode gives tau = 2.76e7 yr and s = -3.6215236e-5 1/kyr. The y axis of the figure reads `Relaxation time (yrs)`.
corrections.action: Read s_j from the .dat file. The converter reads no .mod file.

corrections.field: header line `Harmonic degree, s(1), s(2), ... , s(M) (kyrs)`
corrections.as_shipped: The header gives the unit of s_j as kyrs and says `Total number of modes, M= 12`
corrections.correct: s_j is a frequency in 1/kyr, and the file holds nine modes per degree: the header also says `MAXWELL MODES DELETED FOR PLOTTING`.
corrections.evidence: See spada-t01-01-mod-relaxation-times-in-years: -1000/s_j is the relaxation time in years of the .mod file. Every data row has a degree and nine values.
corrections.action: Take the unit and the mode count from spada_column_layouts.json, not from the header.

corrections.as_shipped: ZM's spectrum has degrees 2 to 5, and the rows of degrees 3 and 4 are byte for byte the row of degree 2
corrections.correct: Not supplied. The spectrum depends on the degree: GS, RR and VB give s_1 = -7.0864376e-5 1/kyr at degree 3, against -3.6215243e-5 at degree 2.
corrections.evidence: The three rows are identical to every printed digit. ZM's Love number files of test 2/1 hold degrees 2 and 5 only, so no ZM value at degree 3 or 4 is used anywhere else.
corrections.action: Keep the rows, so the converted degrees are the degrees printed, and list 3 and 4 in the attribute `degrees_not_to_score`. Scoring skips them.

corrections.field: the order of the nine modes
corrections.as_shipped: ZM lists the modes fastest first: s_1 = -3.358 1/kyr at degree 2. GS, RR and VB list them slowest first: s_1 = -3.62e-5 1/kyr.
corrections.correct: The same modes in the reverse order. The residues of ZM's Love numbers follow ZM's spectrum.
corrections.evidence: In every row of the four spectra the frequencies are strictly monotonic: decreasing for GS, RR and VB, increasing for ZM. Reversed, ZM's degree-2 frequencies agree with GS's to 2e-7 relative, and ZM's h, l and k fluid limits hold with ZM's own order.
corrections.action: Store every member slowest first. The decoder records the order it finds in each file as `mode_order`, and the converter reverses a file that is `fastest_first`.

corrections.as_shipped: RR writes degrees 29 and 40 twice in the spectrum and in each Love number file: 257 rows for 255 degrees
corrections.correct: One row per degree. In the spectrum the two rows are identical. In the Love number files the elastic and fluid values of the two rows are identical, and one residue differs at the level of 1e-12 or less, below the precision of the other residues of that row.
corrections.evidence: Degree 29 of h_L_T01-02_RR.dat has residue 3 as -7.6438776e-12 in one row and -7.7167074e-12 in the other; degree 40 has -2.7734599e-14 and 1.7210357e-15. Both rows satisfy the fluid limit identity to 1e-5 relative.
corrections.action: Keep the first row of a repeated degree when its elastic and fluid values (or, for a spectrum, all values) equal those of the repeat, and raise otherwise. The kept degrees are listed in the attribute `repeated_degrees`.

corrections.as_shipped: VB's residues carry the opposite sign to those of GS, RR and ZM, and each record of twelve values wraps onto a second line after ten values
corrections.correct: The residue in the convention of Spada et al. (2011), h_f = h_e - sum r_j / s_j, is minus the printed value.
corrections.evidence: At degree 2 VB prints the slowest h residue as +3.0189252e-06 and GS as -3.0189264e-06. With the printed sign VB's fluid limit misfits by order one; negated, it holds to 6e-8 relative at every degree in both tests.
corrections.action: Join the lines of a record before splitting it. The decoder finds the sign by the fluid limit at degree 2 and records it as `residue_sign`; the converter multiplies the residues by it.

corrections.as_shipped: Every TABOO profile starts with 16 lines beginning with ` #`, and writes its last row, colatitude 180, twice
corrections.correct: 721 points at 0.25 degree for the cap and the disc, 181 points at 1 degree for the point load
corrections.evidence: All 40 per-epoch files of T02, T02-01 and T02-02 have one more data row than their grid, and the last two rows are identical.
corrections.action: Skip lines that start with `#`. Drop a repeated point with the same values, and raise on a repeated colatitude with different values.

corrections.field: unit of column 2 in the header
corrections.as_shipped: The unit line reads `(deg) (kyrs) (mm/yr) (mm/yr) (mm/yr)`, so column 2, d_rad, is labelled in kyrs
corrections.correct: Column 2 is the vertical displacement rate in mm/yr, as the other three rate columns are
corrections.evidence: T02-02/plot_PAP.gmt draws GS column 2 without a factor on the same axis as VK's vertical rate times 1000, which VK stores in m/yr. The two agree to a few per cent, which fixes the GS unit as mm/yr. A time in kyrs cannot be negative, and column 2 is -77.948066 at the pole at t = 0.
corrections.action: Take the unit from spada_column_layouts.json, which records mm/yr and the header's label.

corrections.as_shipped: Beside the six epoch files of the cap and the disc, the directories hold disp_tinf_cap.dat and rate_tinf_cap.dat (Time 1000 kyr) and disp_t3_disc.dat and rate_t3_disc.dat (Time 3 kyr)
corrections.correct: These are runs with a different load. Their headers give a load mass of 5.793341806542921e18 kg (tinf cap) and 3.874512718475594e18 kg (t3 disc), while the cap and disc of table 4 carry 3.607171340900778e18 kg, which every other file prints. Which load they used is not established.
corrections.evidence: The load mass line of each header. No panel of T02-01/plot_PAP.gmt or T02-02/plot_PAP.gmt reads these four files; the published figure draws disp_t1000_cap.dat and rate_t1000_cap.dat for the last epoch.
corrections.action: Do not convert them. Take the files from the published script, not from a glob.

corrections.as_shipped: The TABOO point load profiles are summed to degree 512 and sampled every degree of colatitude. The file for the last epoch is named tinf and its header says `Time (kyrs) = 1000.000`.
corrections.correct: The case prescribes degrees 2 to 128. A solver truncated at 128 does not reproduce the near field of a point load, where the series converges slowly.
corrections.evidence: The header line of all twelve files. No GMT script in the archive draws them, and no other contributor supplied a point load: T02/output_sec2-from-VOLKER is a parabolic load run and its e2cost files are empty.
corrections.action: Convert them as GS's point load with epochs 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 1000 kyr (the header time, not the name), and record Lmax 512 in an attribute. Compare a solver with them knowing the truncation differs.

corrections.as_shipped: VK stores rates in m/yr (`(m/a)` in the header, `Units are m and m/yr` in the README), while GS stores them in mm/yr
corrections.correct: Both are the same quantity. In the converted files every rate is in m/kyr: VK times 1000, GS unchanged, because 1 mm/yr is 1 m/kyr.
corrections.evidence: T02-02/plot_PAP.gmt draws VK as `$n*1000` and GS as stored on one axis.
corrections.action: Convert with the unit recorded in spada_column_layouts.json, checked against the scale the script applies.

corrections.field: column 5, as plotted in panel 3 of resultsC_2026/figZ_uvf_basin_diff.gmt
corrections.as_shipped: The script divides the VEGA potential by 10 to plot the geoid height.
corrections.correct: Divide by the surface gravity 9.8155, as every other cross-section script for cases A to D does, including the case C script through the ice centre.
corrections.evidence: In case C, YS lies on the same 2048-point colatitude grid as VEGA, so the difference file can be checked with no interpolation. With 9.8155, the largest value of |YS column 6 - VEGA column 5 / g - Z_YS_basin_diff.out column 5| is 1.7e-6 m. With 10, it is 6.2e-3 m. The shipped difference files were therefore computed with 9.8155, and the factor 10 occurs in the plotting script only. The VEGA geoid curve that the script draws through the basin is 1.8 per cent too small in magnitude. It is not known whether the published figure has the same error. A least squares fit over the whole profile gives a gravity of 9.81555 for the difference files of cases B and C, which reduces the largest miss to 6e-9 m. The scripts round it to 9.8155, which changes the geoid by 5e-6 of its size. That is far below the 1.8 per cent of the factor 10.
corrections.action: Take the geoid height as column 5 divided by 9.8155. A reader that follows the script is 1.8 per cent low for VEGA through the case C basin.

corrections.as_shipped: Column 4 is 'ocean area (per cent of 4\pi)'. Column 11 is 'col3-col9'.
corrections.correct: Column 4 is a fraction of 4 pi. Column 11 is column 3 minus column 10, the floating ice mass in 1e18 kg.
corrections.evidence: Column 4 is 0.04628693 at t = 0 in cases C and D. fig_of00D.gmt and fig_of00E.gmt multiply it by 100 to plot per cent, and fig_of00D.gmt draws a reference line at 4.629555 per cent. Column 11 equals column 3 minus column 10 to 1e-8 in all five files. Column 3 minus column 9 would subtract a water thickness in metres from a mass in 1e18 kg. secti.out has no header, and it has the same layout except for column 5; see martinec2018-secti-column5.
corrections.action: Read column 4 as a fraction and column 11 as the floating ice mass. gia_mip/resources/column_layouts.json records both under vega_time_series_format.

corrections.as_shipped: No header. The file has the eleven-column layout of vega76.out, where column 5 is h_UF_1.
corrections.correct: Column 5 holds h_UF_1 + h_UF_4. All other columns are equal to those of resultsD_2026/vega76.out.
corrections.evidence: secti.out and resultsD_2026/vega76.out have the same 751 times. Columns 1 to 4 and 6 to 11 are identical. Column 5 of secti.out equals column 5 plus column 8 of vega76.out to 7e-15 m. As a result, columns 5 to 8 of secti.out do not sum to column 9, and the largest miss is 10.30 m. fig_hufD_secti_detail.gmt reads secti.out and labels column 5 as huf_1.
corrections.action: Read column 5 as h_UF_1 + h_UF_4. For h_UF_1 alone, read vega76.out. Take the total h_UF from column 9 of either file.

corrections.as_shipped: The profile files say 'latitude (degrees_north)' for column 1. The geoid files say 'negative geoidal displacement (m)' for column 2. E2_fig07_1_VK.dat says 'time (day as %Y%)' for column 1.
corrections.correct: Column 1 of the profile files is colatitude in degrees. Column 2 of the geoid files is the geoid displacement, with the sign given on the conventions page. Column 1 of E2_fig07_1_VK.dat is time in kyr.
corrections.evidence: Column 1 of every profile file runs from 0.25 to 179.75, which is outside the range of latitude, and equals column 1 of Z_VK_{load,basin}_diff.out. The case B files from the same code say 'colat'. For the sign: the VK geoid as stored, minus the VEGA geoid, reproduces column 5 of Z_VK_load_diff.out in case C to an RMS of 5.5e-5 m. Negated, the RMS is 1.47 m. The case C basin and both case D profiles give the same result, and the scripts plot the column without negation. Column 1 of E2_fig07_1_VK.dat runs from 0 to 14.9994 in 60 rows.
corrections.action: Read column 1 of a profile file as colatitude and column 2 as it stands. Read column 1 of E2_fig07_1_VK.dat as kyr.

corrections.as_shipped: 'time - huf1 - huf2- huf3 -huf4 // ka - m - m - m -m', which names four components after the time.
corrections.correct: Columns 2, 3 and 4 are three components, and column 5 is their sum, the total h_UF.
corrections.evidence: Column 5 equals column 2 + column 3 + column 4 to 7e-15 m in all 60 rows. fig_hufE.gmt plots column 5 as VK's h_UF against VEGA column 9, the total. The components are not split as VEGA splits them: column 2 is -41.67 m at 15 kyr, which matches VEGA's h_UF_1 + h_UF_4 of -41.67 m and not VEGA's h_UF_1 of -52.16 m.
corrections.action: Read column 5 as the total h_UF. Do not compare columns 2 to 4 with VEGA's components by position.

corrections.field: ice mass, ocean area and h_UF columns
corrections.as_shipped: Each contributor uses its own unit and column order, and most of these files have no header.
corrections.correct: Ice mass in kg, ocean area as a fraction of 4 pi, and h_UF in metres, with the meaning of each column recorded per file.
corrections.evidence: Ice mass is stored in kg by GS, in 1e17 kg by YS, and in 1e18 kg by VEGA, VK and SK. Ocean area is stored as a fraction by VEGA and SK, as a percentage by GS and VK, as ten times a fraction in YS's case D column 3, and as a plain fraction in YS's case E column 3; see martinec2018-ys-case-e-awk-exponent. The plotting scripts compensate with factors of 10, 100 and 1e-17. The order of the two ice mass components differs between YS's case C file (grounded, floating) and case D file (floating, grounded, total), and SK's columns 10 and 11 are in the opposite order to VEGA's. After conversion the contributors agree: in case D the ocean area at t = 0 is 4.615 to 4.631 per cent, and the total ice mass at 15 kyr is 1.184e18 to 1.203e18 kg.
corrections.action: Take the meaning, the unit and the conversion factor of each column from time_series_columns in gia_mip/resources/column_layouts.json. tests/test_layouts.py checks each factor against the scale that the plotting script applies.

corrections.as_shipped: 359 rows. In case D the rows descend from colatitude 179.499 to 0 at a spacing of 180/359 degrees. In the case B basin profile they run from 0.5 to 179.5 at a spacing of 0.5 degrees.
corrections.correct: The difference files Z_*_diff.out for these profiles were computed against a finer VEGA profile, which the archives do not hold.
corrections.evidence: In the case B profile through the ice centre and in both case C profiles, VEGA has 2048 rows on the YS grid, and YS minus VEGA reproduces Z_YS_*_diff.out to 1e-8 m in U. For the three 359-row profiles, a VEGA profile recovered as YS minus the YS difference file on the 2048-point grid agrees with the shipped file at the shipped rows to an RMS of 7.5e-4 m in U for case D through the ice centre, 1.3e-4 m for case D through the basin and 6.9e-4 m for the case B basin. Linear interpolation of the shipped file onto the YS grid misses the recovered profile by up to 0.238 m at colatitude 35.4 for case D through the ice centre, where the ice edge makes U steep, by up to 0.039 m for case D through the basin, and by up to 0.169 m at colatitude 74.2 for the case B basin. As a control, the case C VEGA profile subsampled to 342 rows misses in the same way, by up to 0.255 m. The shipped files therefore behave like coarse copies of the profiles the differences were computed against.
corrections.action: Do not interpolate this file to score against the published difference files. Recover the reference on a contributor's own grid as that contributor's profile minus its difference file, as for benchmark A.

corrections.as_shipped: The row at colatitude 180 is written twice, with identical values, so the file has 1802 rows on a 1801-point grid.
corrections.correct: One row at colatitude 180.
corrections.evidence: In A-fig10-TABOO_256.dat, rows 1801 and 1802 both read colatitude 180.0, U = -2.9071 m, geoid column -0.1803 m, and differ only in the row counter. Z_GS_load_diff.out repeats its last row in the same way. A NetCDF coordinate or an interpolation routine that requires a strictly increasing axis rejects the file.
corrections.action: Drop a point that repeats both the axis value and the data value. Raise if the axis value repeats with a different data value.

corrections.as_shipped: A fraction of 4 pi written with a Fortran D exponent, for example 0.4696086368873D-01. fig_of00E.gmt plots it as $3*10 on a per-cent axis.
corrections.correct: The column is a fraction of 4 pi: 0.04696 at t = 0. The script's factor 10 is right only because awk ignores the exponent.
corrections.evidence: All 151 rows of column 3 carry a D-01 exponent. awk reads 0.4696086368873D-01 as 0.4696086368873, so '$3*10' gives 4.69609, the correct per cent. VEGA column 4 in the same directory is 0.04696366 at t = 0 and 0.04519955 at 15 kyr, and column 3 read with its exponent is 0.04696086 and 0.04520724. The case D file of the same contributor, E2_fig07_YS.dat, writes column 3 with no exponent as 0.4629530185743, which really is ten times the fraction, so the same script factor is right there for a different reason. A unit copied from the case D file makes the converted case E area ten times too small.
corrections.action: Read the exponent. Take the unit from time_series_columns, which records the dropped exponent for this file so that the check against the script still holds.

corrections.as_shipped: The header says `LLN of component k`, and at t = 0 and degree 2 the column holds -0.75601575.
corrections.correct: The column holds -(1 + k): k at t = 0 and degree 2 is -0.24398425.
corrections.evidence: GS's elastic k at degree 2 (test 2/1) is -0.24398316, and -1 minus the printed value is -0.24398425. The k files of T01-05/PAPER/ that figure 6 draws hold -1 minus this column, while the h and l files of the same run copy their columns unchanged.
corrections.action: Do not read the column as k. Read the k files of T01-05/PAPER/, which hold k.

corrections.evidence: VK's VILMA runs start at t = 0 years. T01-05/PAPER/filter.f90 and T01-07/filter.f90 replace a time of 0 by 1e-9 years with `if(time(i)==0.0) time(i)=1E-9` and then divide by 1000, so that a logarithmic axis can take the point. T02-03/LOD/lod.f90 copies the times of k_L_T01-05_VK.mod into lod_VK.dat. The value at that time is the value of the source row at t = 0.
corrections.action: Store the time 1e-12 kyr of these files as 0.

corrections.field: the first rows of every segment
corrections.as_shipped: The h files of test 6/1 start at 0.047532132 kyr, the l and k files of test 6/1 at 0.095064263 kyr, and T01-07/l_Vk.dat at 0.095064263 kyr.
corrections.correct: VK's runs start at t = 0. I107-M3-VSCAb-LLN-[hlk].dat of test 6/1 hold rows at 0 and 47.532132 years before that, and Vk/I106-M3-L70-V01-f1-LLN-l.dat of test 7/1 holds a row at 0.
corrections.evidence: T01-06/FRUFRU.f90 reads 11 lines as header. I107-M3-VSCAb-LLN-h.dat has 10 comment lines and the l and k files have 9, so the program read the first one or two data rows as header and wrote them into the comment lines of the .mod files. Every row it did write equals the source column. T01-07/filter.f90 reads 6 header lines, and VK's l file of test 7/1 has 5.

corrections.as_shipped: The banner comments name GS above the lines that read I106-M3-VSCAb-LLN-[hlk]-VK.mod, and the file names say VK.
corrections.correct: The files are VK's: VILMA runs by Klemann at GFZ.
corrections.evidence: T01-06/FRUFRU.f90, which wrote the files, sets `user_name='VK'` and reads I107-M3-VSCAb-LLN-k.dat, whose header says `performed by spectral FE code, Klemann at GFZ` and `run no.: VEGA-I107`; the .mod files carry the same header lines. In T01-06/love_PAP.gmt the lines that read GS's k_L_T01-05_GS.mod are commented out, and figure 7 of the paper shows Vk, Gsa and Rr only. T01-07/love_PAP.gmt is a copy of the test 6/1 script. The disagreement is listed in attribution_disagreements of spada_column_layouts.json.
corrections.action: Attribute the files to VK by their names. Test 6/1 has no GS data.

corrections.as_shipped: h_Rr.dat and l_Rr.dat are eq. 19 summed over the first six of RR's nine degree-one modes in riva-T01-deg1_inc/.
corrections.correct: The sum over all nine modes. Mode 8, s = -3.3416296 per kyr, has the h residue -1.5084246e-5 and the l residue -7.7171418e-5; modes 7 and 9 are Maxwell modes with residues below 1e-14.
corrections.evidence: T01-07/filter.f90 reads MRR = 9 modes of RR and sums them with `do k=1, mvb`, where MVB = 6. Eq. 19 over six modes reproduces both files to 7e-8; over nine modes the curves differ from the files by at most 4.5e-6 in h and 2.3e-5 in l, at the longest times. The five curves of figure 8 agree to within 5e-3.
corrections.action: Convert the files as figure 8 draws them. The difference is below the agreement between the contributors.

corrections.evidence: Column 3 agrees with GSA's l(t) in Gsa/l-alma-deg1.dat to 1.1e-3 from 1e-3 to 1e4 kyr, as VB's and RR's do. Plotted at zero, GS's l(t) lies outside the axis of figure 8, which runs from -3.25 to -0.75, so the figure shows no GS curve of l although its legend names Gs. h_time_domain.dat has two columns, time and h.
